paper: Miconi, Rawal, Clune & Stanley — Backpropamine
venue_raw: "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2019" (page-1 header, verified; the held copy is the arXiv print, arXiv:2002.10585v1 [cs.NE], 24 Feb 2020)
mechanism_raw: plasticity-modulation — a differentiable three-factor Hebbian rule. Not activation gating: activations are untouched
conditioner: a scalar $M(t)$ computed by the network itself from its own recurrent hidden state, $\tanh$-squashed to $[-1,1]$. In the RL tasks it is an output unit sitting alongside the policy logits and the A2C value head; the hidden state receives previous reward and previous action as inputs, so $M$ can learn to track reward but is never defined as reward
site_raw: the Hebbian trace update of the recurrent weight matrix, i.e. weight-space state, not any activation. RL tasks: one global scalar over all plastic recurrent connections; only the recurrent layer is plastic (input and output weights are ordinary). Basic LM: one modulator neuron per LSTM layer with fan-out to every plastic connection. Large LM: one modulator per LSTM expanded through a per-neuron weight vector to give $\etai$
rl_raw: A2C (advantage actor-critic, meta-training after Wang et al. 2016 L2RL) for tasks 1–2. Task 3 is not RL — supervised language modelling
benchmark: no standard RL benchmark. Two small custom tasks: (1) cue-reward association, 200-step episodes, four random 20-bit cues, 200 recurrent neurons; (2) 9×9 grid-maze foraging with an invisible randomised reward location, 100 recurrent neurons. (3) Penn TreeBank word-level LM, 4.8 M and 24.2 M parameter models
result: Cue-reward: both modulated variants learn the task; non-modulated plastic and non-plastic recurrent nets fail outright (10 runs). Maze: modulated beats non-modulated plasticity, Wilcoxon rank-sum $p<0.05$ at marked points (9 runs). PTB, parameter-matched, 16 runs: baseline LSTM $104.26\pm0.22$ → differentiable plasticity $103.80\pm0.25$ ($p{=}0.0044$) → simple neuromodulation $102.65\pm0.30$ ($p{=}10^{-6}$ vs plasticity) → retroactive $102.48\pm0.28$ ($p{=}10^{-7}$ vs baseline). Large model $62.48 \to 61.44$ (5 runs). Retroactive vs simple is NOT significant ($p{=}0.066$) — the authors say so
claim_raw: ablated — full 4-way ladder (non-plastic / plastic / simple-modulated / retroactive-modulated) on both RL tasks and on LM, with matched trainable-parameter counts (hidden size cut 1150→1149) and per-condition equally-powered grid search. The strongest single result is the Appendix A.5 control: with easy fixed 4-bit cues, non-modulated plasticity does solve the task — isolating "arbitrary high-dimensional cues that must be memorised jointly with the association" as the operative factor. Asserted, not shown: catastrophic-forgetting mitigation (motivating claim, imported from the evolutionary literature — there is no continual-learning experiment in this paper); "self-contained RL algorithm in the weights"; meta-meta-learning; multiple modulatory signals. Modulator-granularity variants (per-node, per-network) are said to perform worse with no numbers reported. Mechanism of the learned $M(t)$ dynamics explicitly declared not understood (App. A.4)

paper: Badia et al. — Agent57: Outperforming the Atari Human Benchmark
venue_raw: No venue line printed in the PDF — ICML-template preprint, arXiv:2003.13350v1, 30 Mar 2020 (no proceedings/copyright footer)
mechanism_raw: one-hot concatenation + scalar output gain — (i) j concatenated as a network input; (ii) Q(x,a,j;θ) = Q(x,a,j;θ^e) + βj·Q(x,a,j;θ^i), i.e. βj is also a literal scalar multiplier on the intrinsic value stream. Not FiLM (one scalar on a whole stream, fixed by the index, not produced by a modulator)
conditioner: one-hot j over N=32 indices, each naming a (βj, γj) pair (Agent57's own wording: "j is a one-hot vector indexing one of N implied MDPs (in particular (βj,γj))"). γ range widened to [0.99, 0.9999] vs NGU's [0.99, 0.997]. New: j is chosen online per episode by a per-actor sliding-window UCB bandit whose reward is the undiscounted extrinsic episode return
site_raw: one-hot: one site, at the recurrent core input, in each of the two networks (App. E inputs verbatim (xs, r^e{s−1}, r^i{s−1}, j, a{s−1}, h{s−1})). Scalar βj: one site, at the output. Two identical-architecture value networks θ^e/θ^i with separate Retrace losses but a shared greedy target policy; intrinsic-reward modules unconditioned
rl_raw: NGU / R2D2 distributed recurrent DQN, transformed Retrace, 256 actors, trace length 160
benchmark: Atari-57 (6 seeds for Agent57, 3 for ablations); 10-game "challenging set"; 15×15 "random coin" gridworld diagnostic
result: First agent above human on all 57 games: capped HNS 100.00, 57/57 games vs NGU 95.07/51, R2D2 94.33/52, MuZero 89.92/51. 5th-percentile HNS 116.67 vs MuZero's 0.03. Skiing took 78 B frames. Agent57 is beaten on uncapped mean and median by MuZero and by R2D2(bandit) — the contribution is the tail. Isolated conditioning result: R2D2(bandit) (discount-index conditioning + bandit, no intrinsic reward) reaches 96.93 CHNS / 54 games vs R2D2(Retrace)'s 94.20 / 52
claim_raw: ablated — each of the three changes separately (separate networks: >20 % CHNS drop when removed; meta-controller: ~20 % CHNS gain on R2D2; BPTT 80 vs 160), plus identity-vs-h-transform mix (no difference) and a purpose-built gridworld diagnostic. The injection operator is never varied (inherited from NGU, asserted). Instability motivating the work, verbatim: NGU "can be unstable and fail to learn ... even in simple environments" when r^e and r^i differ in scale/sparseness/noise; Surround −7.57 → 9.77 with separate networks

paper: Beaulieu, Frati, Miconi, Lehman, Stanley, Clune & Cheney — ANML: Learning to Continually Learn
venue_raw: "Published as a conference paper at ECAI 2020" (page-1 header, verified; 24th European Conference on AI. The held copy is the arXiv print, arXiv:2002.09571v2 [cs.LG], 4 Mar 2020)
mechanism_raw: gating — activation gating by a dedicated side network. Operator is FiLM's multiplicative term with no additive term: $\tilde h = \sigma(g{\theta^{NM}}(x)) \odot h$, gain sigmoid-bounded to $[0,1]$ so it can only suppress — never amplify, never sign-flip (stated verbatim in §3.1). "Selective plasticity" is an indirect consequence: $\partial L/\partial W{cj} \propto \gammaj$, so a gated-off unit's incoming weights stop updating. Nothing touches the learning rule
conditioner: the input image itself — the NM network (3 conv + batchnorm + 1 FC) reads the same image as the prediction network. No task label, no task oracle; removing the oracle is a stated contribution over Masse et al. 2018, which used random, binary, task-label-conditioned masks. Gate is continuous, not binary. NM weights are meta-learned in the outer loop and frozen in the inner loop and at meta-test time — a two-timescale arrangement FiLM does not have
site_raw: exactly one site: the flattened latent representation feeding the prediction network's final fully connected layer. The authors call single-layer gating "a simplifying assumption made in this initial exploration"; a per-synapse variant was built during development, called "competitive", and dropped for compute reasons with no numbers reported
rl_raw: not RL. Entirely supervised continual image classification under a MAML-style meta-learner (inner loop plain SGD, outer loop Adam, backprop through 20 inner steps, 20,000 outer iterations). RL appears once in the whole paper, in future work: "One example is extending the work to reinforcement learning (RL) tasks"
benchmark: Omniglot, 1,623 character classes (963 meta-train / 660 held out). Sequential trajectories of 10–600 classes, 15 instances per class, each image seen once, up to 9,000 SGD updates. ~6 M parameters, matched across all treatments
result: At 600 sequential classes, held-out accuracy ANML 63.8 % vs OML 18.2 % (prior SOTA, same protocol) and OML-OLFT 44.2 %. The load-bearing number is the relative drop from an i.i.d.-trained oracle of the same method — ANML 10 %, OML-OLFT 27.2 %, OML 70.32 %, pretrain-and-transfer 99 %, from-scratch 99 % — which isolates forgetting from raw capacity. Sequentially trained ANML beats the i.i.d. oracles of every other method ($p \le 1.93\times10^{-23}$). Gating drops active units 52.77 % → 5.9 % while OML sits at 3.89 %, i.e. ANML forgets less with a less sparse representation; 0 % dead neurons for both. KNN on the gate's own output classifies unseen characters at 70.9 % vs 24.3 % for a random-weight NM network of identical architecture
claim_raw: ablated, thoroughly, with one important gap. 10 meta-trained models × 10 meta-test trajectories per treatment, Mann-Whitney U throughout, per-sequence-length LR search, parameter count matched, i.i.d. oracle for every arm, multi-epoch check (Fig. S7), freezing/unfreezing ablation (Fig. S8), and a proper random-weight null for the KNN probe. The gap: there is no continual-learning arm in which the NM network is replaced by a static, random, or task-conditioned mask — the random-weight NM appears only in the KNN probe. So "ANML beats OML" and "the gate's output is informative" are established; "the gain comes from the gate being meta-learned and input-conditioned rather than merely present" is not directly isolated. Second confound: ANML has batchnorm and the controls do not (batchnorm was found to hurt OML, so it was removed), so ANML differs from its baseline in two ways. Also asserted, not shown: that gating "can easily be extended to any and all layers"; the $[0,1]$ suppress-only range is never compared against a $\tanh$ alternative; and the authors state outright that why ANML also wins in the i.i.d. multi-epoch setting — where there is no forgetting to prevent — is an open question, which means the paper's own causal story does not explain its strongest result

paper: Ferguson & Cardin — Mechanisms underlying gain modulation in the cortex
mechanism_raw: other — biology review; establishes the divisive (gain) vs additive (offset) distinction
conditioner: attention, arousal, locomotion, learning, and the four classical neuromodulators

result: Gain is dQ/dI. This is the substrate every DNN neuromodulation paper appeals to

paper: Brohan et al., RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
venue_raw: "Preprint" (running header on every page); arXiv:2212.06817v2 [cs.RO] 11 Aug 2023. No conference/journal line printed — the usual "RSS 2023" attribution is not verifiable from this file
mechanism_raw: Identity-initialized full affine FiLM, printed in Fig. 1(a) as (1+γ)·x + β, with the dense layers (fc, hC) producing γ and β zero-initialized so the layer starts as the exact identity and does not destroy the pretrained backbone

Named hazard: inserting FiLM into a pretrained net "would disrupt the intermediate activations and negate the benefit of using pretrained weights" — solved by identity init; removing ImageNet pretraining costs −33 on unseen tasks

The early-FiLM-fusion-vs-Gato's-late-fusion argument (App. D.5) is a hypothesis with attention-map support, confounded by 3 other architectural differences, and BC-Z also uses FiLM

paper: Beck, Vuorio, Xiong & Whiteson — Recurrent Hypernetworks are Surprisingly Strong in Meta-RL
venue_raw: "37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)" (page-1 footer); arXiv:2309.14970v4, 26 Dec 2023. Distinct from the already-held Beck et al. Hypernetworks in Meta-Reinforcement Learning, whose footer prints "6th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2022), Auckland, New Zealand" — different author list (Jackson vs Xiong) and different contribution
mechanism_raw: hypernet — full weight generation: a GRU emits all weights and biases of the feed-forward policy, regenerated every timestep. Bias-HyperInit (final hypernet layer = zero weight matrix + non-zero bias, so the generator is constant at step 0)
conditioner: the full agent history (states, actions, rewards) across the meta-episode, summarised by a single 256-unit GRU. Not a task label; changes each timestep. The raw state is additionally fed straight to the generated policy
site_raw: the entire feed-forward policy (state embedding 256, MLP 256→128)
rl_raw: PPO (on-policy meta-RL; VariBAD/Beck-2022 codebase defaults). Policy-gradient meta-RL methods excluded by design
benchmark: Grid-World / Grid-World Show / Grid-World Dense (5×5); MuJoCo Cheetah-Dir, Cheetah-Vel, Ant-Dir, Walker (65 physics params); MineCraft MC-LS long-term visual memory; Meta-World ML10 (appendix)
result: RNN+HN is the strongest method evaluated, beating four task-inference baselines given equal tuning compute: best asymptotic return and sample efficiency on all three grid-worlds (incl. the one designed to disadvantage it); wide-margin wins on Cheetah-Dir and Ant-Dir; tie on Cheetah-Vel; small loss on Walker; significant win over VI+HN on MineCraft. Plain RNN fails outright on Walker and Cheetah-Dir. Two mechanism claims: (a) Kaiming-initialised RNN+HN is among the worst methods — init is decisive; (b) the RNN+S control (state fed in twice, no hypernet) closes part but not all of the gap — authors' explicit conclusion is "re-conditioning on state directly is not sufficient, and the hypernetwork architecture itself is still critical". Latent-gradient-norm analysis (preliminary): worst models have the highest norm. No FiLM baseline anywhere in this paper; ML10 is the only numeric result and is reported as a match, not a win (RNN+HN 17.22 % vs VI+HN 13.87 % test success, CIs overlapping)
claim_raw: ablated (RNN vs RNN+S vs RNN+HN; Bias-HyperInit vs Kaiming; 4 task-inference baselines + 5 further appendix ablations; equal tuning budget). Caveats: 3 seeds, learning rate maxed over 5 values, all main results are learning curves with no numeric table, gradient analysis explicitly labelled preliminary

venue_raw: "37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)" printed on p. 1; arXiv:2310.16661v1 [cs.AI] 25 Oct 2023
mechanism_raw: Hypernetwork generates the weights of a bottleneck adapter (256→32→256) spliced between layers, with residual skip: θA = H(c), x ← x + A(x\
conditioner: θA). Rung 2 (low-rank adapter, generated weights). Proved to strictly contain FiLM/cGate (W = diag(g(c)) recovers the elementwise gate). Hypernetwork uses chunking: ≈16 k params vs ≈1.7 M unchunked
site_raw: Ground-truth context, GIVEN — episode-constant physical dynamics parameters (ODE coefficients; CartPole gravity/cart mass/pole mass/pole length/force; Ant mass), per-dimension normalised by the largest training value. Never inferred from transitions (named as future work)
rl_raw: Both actor and critic. Default: actor — between trunk and action head (pre-activation); critic — before its last layer. Location ablation shows input-layer and output-layer placement both fail; middle-of-network works; 3 adapters ≈ 1
benchmark: SAC (CleanRL, PyTorch), identical for all five arms; parameter counts equalised across architectures; 16 seeds
result: ODE (1-D and 2-D context), CartPole (pole length + k distractor dims), MuJoCo Ant (mass, 111-d obs)
claim_raw: Conditional, and that is the point. With clean fully-relevant context all context-aware arms tie (CartPole k=0, all ≈ optimal 500). With irrelevant context dimensions whose values shift train→test, Concat and cGate collapse while the Adapter is stable — Adapter with 100 distractors beats Concat with 20; same on Ant. Where context is necessary (2-D ODE AER): Adapter 159.0 > Concat 109.0 > cGate 85.0 > FLAP 60.0. Removing the hypernetwork (AdapterNoHnet) "performs much worse"; cGate at every layer ≠ better than cGate at one

paper: Chi et al., Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
venue_raw: No venue line printed in the PDF — SAGE-journal two-column layout (Abstract + Keywords, running header "Diffusion Policy"), stamped arXiv:2303.04137v5 [cs.RO] 14 Mar 2024. The "RSS 2023 / IJRR" attribution is not verifiable from this file
mechanism_raw: Full affine FiLM (a·x + b, two Linear layers), applied channel-wise at every convolution layer of the denoising U-Net; cites Perez et al. 2018 by name. Transformer variant replaces it with multi-head cross-attention
conditioner: Observation embedding Ot + denoising iteration k. Ot = last To≈2 frames through per-view ResNet-18 (spatial-softmax, GroupNorm, no pretraining, trained end-to-end) concatenated with proprioception. Recomputed every control step and every denoising step — the corpus's only fast, observation-derived conditioner
site_raw: The action-denoising network εθ (1-D temporal CNN over the action sequence). Modulation is the ONLY path by which the observation reaches it — no concat, no skip. Not an encoder, no critic exists
rl_raw: not RL — behavior cloning / imitation learning, loss = MSE(ε^k, εθ(Ot, A⁰t+ε^k, k)). Limitations section names RL as future work
benchmark: 15 tasks / 4 benchmarks: Robomimic (Lift, Can, Square, Transport, ToolHang; ph+mh; state & image), Push-T, Multimodal Block Push, Franka Kitchen; plus real single-arm and bimanual tasks
result: +46.9 % average success over prior SOTA imitation learning. Conditioning-relevant: FiLM-CNN vs cross-attention transformer flips with conditioner modality — image conditioner → FiLM wins (ToolHang 0.73 vs 0.47, Transport-mh 0.69 vs 0.50, Push-T 0.84 vs 0.66 on last-10 avg); low-dim state conditioner → attention wins (state ToolHang 0.87 vs 0.30, BlockPush p2 0.94 vs 0.11). Failure mode: FiLM-CNN "performs poorly when the desired action sequence changes quickly and sharply" (velocity control) — temporal-conv low-frequency bias. BatchNorm→GroupNorm required for stability under EMA
claim_raw: asserted for the mechanism claim — "FiLM conditioning … is better than inpainting on all tasks except Push-T" (Appendix A.4) is given with no numbers, and the state-based Push-T DiffusionPolicy-C cell in Tab. 1 used inpainting, not FiLM. Never compared to concatenation. The C-vs-T comparison IS numeric but confounds backbone with conditioning route

paper: Xiong, Beck & Whiteson — Universal Morphology Control via Contextual Modulation (ModuMorph)
venue_raw: "Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, Honolulu, Hawaii, USA. PMLR 202, 2023" printed in the p. 1 footer; arXiv:2203.01110v2 [cs.AI] 3 Aug 2023
mechanism_raw: Two operators, ablated separately. (1) HN — full weight generation of the per-limb linear layers: W^ik, b^ik = HNφ(c^ik), rung 3; transformer trunk NOT generated ("too many weight matrices"). (2) FA — fixed attention: key and query come from a context encoder, value from the node embedding, so the attention matrix depends on morphology alone and is constant within an episode (a routing modulation, off the affine spectrum). No FiLM arm exists; the paper instead shows the concat baseline is an additive-bias modulator (FiLM with gain frozen at 1)
conditioner: Given, not inferred. Per-limb morphology context from the UNIMAL benchmark — limb size, mass, initial position relative to parent — plus the tree adjacency matrix. Time-invariant. Two separate MLP context encoders (2-layer for HN, 3-layer for FA, 128 units)
site_raw: Base controller: per-node embedding layer and per-node decoder (weights + biases generated); transformer encoder attention matrices (K/Q replaced by context embeddings). Trunk weights untouched. Critic architecture never stated in the PDF despite the paper's worst result being a value-prediction failure
rl_raw: PPO (on-policy), MetaMorph setup; early-stopping KL threshold tuned per method per environment over {0.03, 0.05}; 3 seeds
benchmark: UNIMAL — 100 train + 100 held-out morphologies, five environments (Flat terrain, Incline, Exploration, Variable terrain, Obstacles); 100 M steps (first three) / 200 M steps (last two)
result: vs. the same backbone (MetaMorph): training final return +19/53/48/31/29 %; zero-shot to kinematics-dynamics variation +26/50/43/28/30 %; zero-shot to unseen topologies +18/29/24/27/37 % (Table 1: Obstacles 1133±12 vs 829±50). The ablation dissociates the two operators (counts below from Table 1, unseen topologies; §5.1 reports HN helping in 3/5 during training): FA improves in 5/5 environments and never hurts; HN helps in only 2/5, is neutral in 2/5, and actively harms Exploration (16±3 vs 19±1) — diagnosed as much higher value-prediction error under partial observability. On Incline, FA alone (468±58) beats FA+HN (403±66). Negative result: feeding the fast terrain height map into the attention computation was worse than baseline
claim_raw: Ablated — 5 arms × 5 environments × 3 seeds with Welch's t-test, plus a motivating single-robot proof-of-concept and a baseline audit (App. C) showing MetaMorph's reported positional-encoding gain is really an artefact of an inconsistent-dropout bug acting as an accidental trust region. Weakened by 3 seeds, large across-seed variance, and per-arm hyperparameter tuning

mechanism_raw: Three hypernetworks (policy + 2 critics, plus target copies) each emit the FULL parameter set of a 1-hidden-layer (256-unit) main network: weights W, biases b, AND per-unit multiplicative gains g, per layer. Main layer computes ReLU((1+g)⊙z W + b) — a generated FiLM-style gain wrapped inside full weight generation. Hypernet body = 3 blocks, each a linear layer + 2 residual blocks (arch + init taken from Sarafian et al.); main-net arch from Littwin & Wolf 2019. result: Wins all 8 train/eval cells vs 4 TD3 variants. Against the loss-matched TD3(Huber) baseline — the correct comparison — evaluation reward improves 1.38x to 1.55x: KS −175.33±20.85 vs −249.76±37.31; parametric KS −210.50±18.04 vs −326.36±30.47; gyre −39.16±6.00 vs −57.55±10.82; parametric gyre −110.06±16.05 vs −152.05±43.72. vs plain concatenation-TD3 the gap is 1.7x-3.9x (parametric gyre −110.06 vs −430.34). Baseline design is genuinely good — separate controls for the loss change (TD3-Huber), the main-network depth (TD3-2layers), and the need for parameters at all (TD3-no-µ). But: "generalization to unseen scenarios" is NOT demonstrated — training and evaluation draw µ from the SAME uniform distribution, with no held-out or extrapolation range, unlike HyPoGen's disjoint splits or CASH's OOD teams. The generated FiLM-style gain g is never ablated, so the FiLM-vs-full-weight-generation split is untested in the one architecture that contains both. Two independent entanglement ablations (FuPS+ID (No State) at the monolithic level, w/o GD at the generator level), plus a 40M-step control and a parameter-matched control. But: Eq. (11) is a factorization identity, not an inequality — no proof that variance is lower is given; the variance measurement is one bar chart on one toy env with no number in the text; and w/o GD is never scored on the variance metric, so ablation and mechanism are never joined. w/o GD also silently changes weight-regeneration frequency from per-iteration to per-timestep — an unacknowledged second manipulation

paper: Yao et al. (Zhou, Yao, Luo, Zhou, Yang), Hyper-GoalNet: Goal-Conditioned Manipulation Policy Learning with HyperNetworks
venue_raw: "39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)" printed on p.1; arXiv:2512.00085v1 [cs.RO] 26 Nov 2025
mechanism_raw: Full weight generation of a small policy head using the HyPoGen iterative-optimization hypernetwork (8 blocks, theta^k = theta^{k-1} + lambda^k psi^k). Static R3M visual encoder, proprio encoder and latent dynamics model are NOT generated. Plus two auxiliary latent-shaping losses: forward-dynamics prediction and a hinge loss forcing monotonic decrease of latent distance to goal (margin beta=0 suffices)

site_raw: All weights of a 3-layer MLP target policy that consumes a 2-frame observation window plus proprioception; the policy never sees the goal again
rl_raw: Not RL — reward-free behavior cloning, stated explicitly in Appendix D. Paper notes prior robotic hypernetwork work is RL-based and "not directly adaptable"
benchmark: Robosuite / MimicGen, 16 tasks: contact-rich (Coffee, Mug-cleanup, Three-piece assembly, Threading, Nut assembly) and long-horizon (Coffee Preparation, Kitchen), difficulty levels d0-d2; 950 demos/task, 50 rollouts/eval; plus real 7-DoF RealMan arm, 4 tasks x 15 trials

Goal-only variant (G) reaches 0.50 (vs 0.52) at 1.46 ms/step vs C-BeT's 13.61 ms. vs HyperZero given two stabilizing init schemes: 77% vs 16% / 16% on Coffee
claim_raw: Mixed. Mechanism claim is well ablated at the joint level: shaping removed 0.77→0.31; the transplant "C-BeT + our shaping" = 0.69 vs ours 0.77 isolates the conditioning mechanism with representation held fixed; HyperZero comparison controls hyperparameters and varies only the hypernetwork. The two latent constraints are ablated only JOINTLY — no row removes the forward-dynamics loss alone or the distance loss alone (only variants: start-anchored 0.45, cosine 0.59). GCBC/Play-LMP scoring exactly 0.00 on all 16 tasks is diagnosed as a log-likelihood-objective failure by argument, not by a same-objective control. No FiLM baseline.

paper: Zhu et al. — EquAct (iFiLM)
venue_raw: unstated — the PDF says "Preprint. Under review." "ICLR 2026 Poster" comes from an external OpenReview record under a slightly different title (§5.2 R5)
mechanism_raw: FiLM, symmetry-constrained — "iFiLM"; the corpus's only genuinely grouped modulation
conditioner: language-instruction embedding (CLIP tokenizer → transformer), treated as a rotation-invariant scalar
site_raw: inside the SE(3)-equivariant Point Transformer U-Net trunk; site count not enumerated in the PDF

benchmark: 18 RLBench tasks with 249 language variations + 4 physical tasks

paper: Benad, Banerjee, Röder, Ay, Butz & Eppe — Dynamics-Aligned Shared Hypernetworks for Contextual RL under Discontinuous Shifts (DMA\-SH)
venue_raw: "Preprint." — printed verbatim on p. 1; arXiv:2602.06550v2 [cs.LG] 11 May 2026; PDF metadata DOI is the arXiv DOI (10.48550/arXiv.2602.06550). ⚠ The PDF contains no ICLR 2026 statement — no acceptance banner, no proceedings style. Cite as a preprint unless acceptance is confirmed venue-side
mechanism_raw: Hypernetwork-generated bottleneck adapter, rung 2, operator identical to the Decision Adapter: x̃ = x + Wup(ω)·ReLU(Wdown(ω)x), trunk 256 → bottleneck 32 → 256, residual skip, no pre-adapter activation. Two novelties, both ablated: the generated weights ω are shared by the dynamics model, the actor and the critic; and ω is trained only by forward-dynamics reconstruction, with a stop-gradient blocking RL losses
conditioner: INFERRED from transitions — the only such paper in this batch. A window of the last K transitions (st, at, δs{t+1}) (K=24 toy / 128 DMC-Gym; a random 20 % subsample, shuffled) → 40 % random input masking → AvgL1Norm → LSTM → 8-dim code → SimNorm (two 4-way simplices). Trained by ‖δŝ{t+1} − δs{t+1}‖². Ground truth is never given to the method (the Concat and Decision-Adapter baselines DO get it)
site_raw: One adapter per network, after the feature trunk and before the output head, in all three of fθ (dynamics), πξ (actor) and Qζ (critic) — with the same generated weights in all three
rl_raw: SAC (CleanRL defaults, untuned) for every arm except the recurrent Amago baseline; 10 seeds, 20 contexts per split, IQM + bootstrap CIs (rliable)
benchmark: Actuator Inversion Benchmark (AIB), introduced here: 14 environments (custom + DeepMind Control + Gymnasium), each with 2 context dims, split into overlapping (mass, gravity, friction) and non-overlapping (binary actuator sign-flip c ∈ {±1}, actuator permutation q ∈ {0,1}); three disjoint context sets (train / interpolation / extrapolation)
result: Conditional on regime, mirroring Beukman. Held-out (eval-out) relative gains: +58.1 % vs. domain randomisation, +11.5 % vs. Concat, +4.6 % vs. the Decision Adapter — but split by type, overlap: +7.3/+5.4/+1.7 % vs. non-overlap: +97.3/+14.1/+5.8 %. Architecture-only step (inferred code held fixed) DMA\→DMA\-SH: 0.64→0.68 all, 0.68→0.73 non-overlap. Ask (a): shared beats separate (DMA\-H) on all three splits, and costs +4.1 % params vs. DA while training 43.5 % faster with 24.4 % less memory; shadow-gradient diagnostic shows the shared design keeps the policy far more sensitive to context than the separate one. Ask (b): yes, ablated — removing dynamics alignment (DMA\-H RL-only, ≈ R2PGO) underperforms, and letting actor gradients into the shared hypernetwork gives near-zero returns
claim_raw: Ablated, thoroughly — component ablations by probability-of-improvement (masking / input norm / output norm and all combinations), sweeps over masking ratio, 4 input norms, 3 output norms, 6 window sizes, and a 7-arm architecture ablation isolating sharing, dynamics alignment, and actor/critic gradient detachment. Weakened by: no comparison of dynamics prediction against other self-supervised objectives; the noise-robustness claim (Remark A.6) is argued but never measured — and Beukman's measurement points the other way at high noise

paper: Büchi et al. — Events as Triggers for Behavioral Diversity in MARL
venue_raw: "Preprint." — no venue printed (arXiv:2605.12388v2 [cs.MA]). Method is unnamed in the text; anonymised repo slug hyperscale-48D6
mechanism_raw: Low-rank additive residual + a global scalar gain — the rung between FiLM and full weight generation. $zm = W{\text{shared}}\phi(ot) + \alpha DmCm\phi(ot)$ with $Cm\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}$, $Dm\in\mathbb{R}^{da\times r}$, rank 8. Additive in pre-activation space, not per-channel multiplicative, so not FiLM; but the shared backbone is kept, so not full generation either. $\alpha$ is not generated — it is a per-batch normalisation ratio $\mathrm{NMD}{\text{des}}/\widehat{\mathrm{NMD}}$, i.e. an automatic gain control on the modulation path
conditioner: All three of: one token per agent from that agent's local observation $o{i,t}$; the event encoding $et$; and the target diversity scalar NMDdes. Generator is a 2-block / 2-head transformer, embed 64, MLP hidden 256. Centralised (needs all agents' observations). Critically, the generator is queried only when an event fires, and the adapter is frozen between events
site_raw: Final linear layer of the policy only — one site, actor side. Critic is not modulated (separate [128,128] MAPPO critic). Backbone [128,128]. Final-layer placement is load-bearing for the theory: any nonlinearity between the LoRA update and the policy mean forfeits the exact diversity-scaling result
rl_raw: MAPPO (on-policy, centralised critic). $10^7$ steps ($1.5\times10^8$ Football), 128 parallel envs, LR 6e-4
benchmark: Six VMAS tasks: Reverse Transport, Navigation, Dispersion, Football (3v heuristic), plus two custom — Pressure Plate (sequential 3-phase, 2 plates + door) and Wind Flocking. 5 seeds, evaluated at best checkpoint, not final. Baselines: HyperMARL, CASH, DiCo (SND grid-searched per task), full parameter sharing
result: Football: ~98 % completion vs 0 % for all four baselines [digitized, Fig. 2d]. Dispersion 99 vs HyperMARL 65.5 / CASH 33 / DiCo 85 / PS 50.5; Navigation 96 vs 69 / 95.5 / 91 / 84.5 [digitized]. Pressure Plate: 98.5 % vs 0 % for the single-query ablation and for all four baselines — the event trigger is worth the entire task. Survives mid-episode agent removal: Football 98.2 → 88.6 %, Pressure Plate 98.4 → 81.2 % (Table 4c, the only printed numbers). LoRA rank sweep $r\in\{2,4,8,16,32,64\}$ shows no separation — 32× capacity range, flat
claim_raw: Mixed. Ablated: the event trigger (single-query control, same architecture, 98.5 → 0 %) and the rank sweep. Asserted: "low-rank stabilises optimisation relative to dense matrices" (no dense control); "per-step regeneration is unstable" (attribution about the CASH baseline, not a within-architecture test); final-layer placement (no alternative site tried). Theory: Thm. 3's projection is proved but Step 2 silently drops a transpose ($P$ is oblique, not symmetric); Corollary 4's displayed limit $I-\frac{B(B-1)}{2}\hat u\hat u^\top$ is not a projector for $B>2$ — the normalisation is dropped from $\nabla\widehat{\mathrm{NMD}}$ but kept in $\widehat{\mathrm{NMD}}$; the stated conclusion ($I-\hat u\hat u^\top$) is right and the display is wrong. Lemma 6's Gaussian assumption fails in the implemented system ($\tanh$-squashed policies); App. B.5 concedes this and degrades the identity to a Lipschitz bound. Two sentences in §5.2 misdescribe the paper's own Fig. 2 — cite the figure, not the prose

paper: Marquis & Farhood
venue_raw: unstated (arXiv 2604.03392v1); IEEE two-column format, no venue line
mechanism_raw: FiLM vs hypernetwork-LoRA, head-to-head (both generated by a hypernetwork)

paper: Morissette et al., Tactile Modality Fusion for Vision-Language-Action Models (TacFiLM)
venue_raw: No venue line printed in the PDF — Springer LNCS layout, running head "C. Morissette et al."; stamped arXiv:2603.14604v2 [cs.RO] 15 Jul 2026. "ECCV 2026" is not verifiable from this file. Printed title carries no "TacFiLM:" prefix
mechanism_raw: Full affine FiLM in identity form: FiLM(Fn given γn, βn) = Fn ⊙ (1 + γn) + βn, γ,β zero-initialized, produced by an MLP; applied after normalization, before multi-head self-attention in ViT blocks; γ,β broadcast over the whole feature map (per-channel, shared across patch tokens)
conditioner: Pooled tactile embedding zt from a DIGIT vision-based touch sensor, encoded by a frozen pretrained tactile model (Sparsh-DINO; T3 / Sparsh-MAE / Sparsh-IJEPA also evaluated), patch features averaged. Recomputed every timestep — a fast, exogenous second sensory modality, not language and not the visual observation
site_raw: The visual backbone of the VLA (fused SigLIP + DINOv2), all ViT blocks by default; ablated to early / middle / late thirds. Llama-2 7B decoder and MLP action head are unmodulated; no critic
rl_raw: not RL — imitation learning: 80 teleoperated demos per task, L1 regression on continuous action chunks, LoRA finetuning of VLA + tactile linear layers with FiLM layers trained from scratch, 80 k steps
benchmark: Real Franka Emika Panda, DIGIT tactile sensor; 9 contact-rich tasks (Circle/Square/Pentagon peg insertion at 2 mm and 3 mm clearance, USB and HDMI cable plugging, drawer opening); >1000 rollouts (480 ID, 300 OOD, 240 ablation)
result: The corpus's cleanest FiLM vs concatenation vs cross-attention head-to-head. ID average success: TacFiLM 86.7 % vs TactileConcat 64.8 % vs vision-only 58.1 % vs Cross-Attn 48.0 %. OOD average: 86.7 % vs 73.3 % vs 54.7 % vs 49.3 %. Concatenation is worse than no tactile on Open-Drawer (26.7 vs 33.3); cross-attention loses everywhere. First-attempt ("direct") rate 29.3 % vs 8.0 % vs 0.0 % OOD. Peak force ~1/3 of baselines (Square-Peg 2 mm: 7.1 N vs 27.7 / 26.2 / 34.3 N). Holds 100 % success under 80 % dimmed lighting and 50 % frozen frames. Depth sweep: early/middle/late third ≈ all blocks. Reported failure modes are the alternatives' — cross-attention hypothesised data-hungry; concatenation's force rises under distribution shift
claim_raw: ablated — fusion mechanism is the controlled variable on a shared OpenVLA-OFT backbone and shared tactile encoder, explicitly "so that differences in performance can be attributed to the fusion strategy rather than the underlying architecture"; plus an injection-depth ablation and a visual-degradation stress test. Caveats: imitation learning not RL; small data (80 demos/task), which the authors themselves say may explain cross-attention's failure

paper: Yoon, Jeong et al. — PAPL
venue_raw: unstated (arXiv 2602.09370v2). "ICRA 2026" appears only in the arXiv comments field, not the PDF (§5.2 R5)
